newsitem.title: GERMANY: Waigel says still expects 96 deficit at 74 bln dm.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says still expects 96 deficit at 74 bln dm.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel expects the final government deficit to total about 73-74 billion marks ($47.1-47.7 billion), as he predicted in November, according to an interview with German television.

Waigel also said in the interview with Germany's n-tv, which was to be broadcast on Sunday night, that he would wait for important economic data before deciding whether to push for a budget freeze in 1997 in addition to the final 1996 results.
"I am reserving all possibilities," Waigel was quoted as saying in the interview, in a statement issued by the network.

Waigel also said he has sent letters to ministries at the end of 1996 about budget plans for 1997 and the further need for consolidation efforts as Germany seeks to meet criteria to join European monetary union, slated to begin in January 1999.
In addition, Waigel said efforts to reform German income taxes must come only in two stages instead of one measure in order to shore up budget shortfalls from lower taxes. ($1=1.5492 Mark)
